subject: GPU SKU tradeoffs, perf/$ sensitivity and phased-commit exchange proposal
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@datascalelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@datascalelabs.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + SKU tradeoffs (A100/H100/L40S)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call this morning. Following up with our ask so you can put together a formal cost/throughput comparison and a sample reserved-commit structure we can take to procurement. Key points from our side: 

- Primary workload: conversational summarization + embedding indexes (seq len ~512, peak 2–3k qps burst, sustained 400 qps).
- We'd like 99th percentile tail latency under 150ms for generation on a 4k context-equivalent path (we know tokenization varies).
- Interested in perf/$ sensitivity across A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), and L40S (48GB). We care about memory for large KV-caches and perf at smaller batch sizes.
- Curious about: (a) how throughput SLOs map to reserved GPU counts, (b) how Redwood prices SKU exchanges mid-term, and (c) whether you offer a phased commit with trial pool before full commit.

I've attached a short throughput-request PDF with representative traces and our expected model mix. Procurement looped in for commercial.

Appreciate a concise proposal (numbers + a headline option) that shows: baseline monthly cost, effective perf/$, recommended SKU mix, and an option for a 9- vs 12-month commit.

—Alex
DataScale Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@datascalelabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + SKU tradeoffs (A100/H100/L40S)

Alex — thanks, this is very clear. I pulled the traces and the ask into a quick internal note and attached a small set of benchmark hits we ran yesterday against a representative mix (see throughput-benchmarks-9-12.pdf).

High level next steps:
1) We'll map your traces against our queue/batching model to produce an estimated reserved GPU count for each SKU (A100/H100/L40S) and show cost per effective token and perf/$ for your mix.
2) I'll propose two commercial structures: a rolling phasing (small trial pool -> staggered ramp -> full reserved commit) and a straight 9/12 month upfront commit with tiered discounts.
3) We'll include an SKU-exchange clause that allows up to 20% quarter-over-quarter SKU swaps with a 60-day notice and re-benchmarking; pricing delta will be handled via an agreed perf/$ true-up.

Could you confirm: expected median sequence length, percent of chat vs embed calls, and whether model size skew (our runs assume majority 13B-class + 70% generation / 30% embedding)? That'll help us pick batch windows.

I'll get a formal offer over in 48 hours.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-13T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing approach / SKU-exchange playbook (DataScale Labs)

Team — quick notes (internal). Alex sent good telemetry; procurement will want concrete dollars + low-risk rollback mechanics. My recommendation:

- Commercial framing: give them two options (Baseline: 9-month reserved commit; Premium: 12-month with extra discount and an early-exchange credit).
- Pricing mechanics: show per-GPU nominal list, then an effective perf/$ metric (tokens per dollar) at their burst profile. H100 wins on tokens/sec for generation-heavy jobs but costs ~30–40% more list than A100; L40S is attractive for embedding-heavy, high-concurrency patterns because of throughput per-dollar at smaller contexts.
- Credits & SLOs: commit a soft throughput SLO (monthly throughput target); if we miss SLO for >2 months we credit usage (slot-hours) at the committed rate. No instant refunds—credits applied to future invoices.
- SKU exchange: allow up to 20% of pool to be shifted per quarter with 60-day notice. If they want >20%, we treat it as re-pricing and run a re-benchmark; include a one-time engineering revalidation fee for >40% swaps within 6 months.
- Phasing/trial: push a 30–45 day pilot (small pool ~5 GPUs) at a reduced committed rate (50% of headcount billed as reserved credit), then ramp. Pilot reduces procurement friction.

Numbers suggestion (ballpark for proposal rows):
- A100 40GB: list $X, effective perf/$ baseline = Y tokens/$ (we'll fill exacts after bench).
- H100 80GB: list $X+30%, perf improvement +40% at generation-heavy paths.
- L40S 48GB: list $X-15%, perf edge on small batches/embeds.

Vivek — can you produce a 9/12 month discount matrix and a trial pool billing stub I can send tomorrow? Laura — any legal clauses we should avoid putting in the initial offer (e.g., penalties that procurement may object to)?

—V
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@datascalelabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@datascalelabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood commercial offer — DataScale Labs (DL-7834)

Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise commercial offer (redwood-offer-v2.xlsx) and an appendix describing the benchmark assumptions. Key headline terms below: 

1) Structure: 3-stage phased commit: Pilot (30d small pool), Ramp (3 months staged increase), Full Commit (remainder to reach committed pool). Pilot pool billed as 50% credited reserved hours to reduce ramp risk.

2) SKU mix options (sample):
   - Conservative: 60% A100 (40GB) / 40% L40S (48GB) — favors predictability, lower list cost.
   - Performance: 70% H100 (80GB) / 30% A100 — favors tail latency & generation throughput.
   - Embed-first: 80% L40S / 20% A100 — minimizes perf/$ for embedding-heavy patterns.

3) Throughput SLOs & credits: Monthly throughput target set by agreed traces. If monthly throughput falls below target by >10% for two consecutive months, Redwood issues a credit equal to 10% of that month’s reserved fee for each month missed (applied to next invoice).

4) SKU exchange clause: Up to 20% of pool may be exchanged per quarter with 60-day notice. Exchanges within 40% of pool within 6 months will require a re-benchmark and a one-time engineering validation fee (listed in the attached workbook).

5) Pricing & discounts: Two pricing rows in the sheet — 9-month commit (baseline discounts) and 12-month commit (additional 7% on top of baseline). If DataScale elects immediate 12-month commit, we can extend an additional 5% credit for early invoicing (applies to first quarter). Detailed per-GPU rates are in the attached workbook.

6) Trial request: We can start a 30-day pilot within 7 business days of signed SOW. Pilot is non-billable for usage but billed at a reduced reserved-credit rate to reserve capacity.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 45-minute walkthrough tomorrow to go through the sheet and align on the SKU mix?

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-offer-v2.xlsx; throughput-benchmarks-9-12.pdf
From: Procurement <procurement@datascalelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@datascalelabs.com>
Date: 2028-09-15T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial offer — DataScale Labs (DL-7834)

Vanessa — thanks for the detailed packet. A few procurement items before we set a walkthrough: 

- Procurement would prefer a 30-day pilot with no reserved billing (pure evaluation) rather than a partly-billed pilot. Is that something Redwood will consider?
- We're open to a 12-month commit but would need an additional 10% on top of the baseline discount you proposed (so a larger incentive to lock). If Redwood can meet that, we're prepared to move faster.
- Please call out any termination windows and whether credits are refundable or strictly future invoice credits.

Alex — I'll review the workbook and schedule a time.

Procurement Team
DataScale Labs
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@datascalelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-15T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial offer — DataScale Labs (DL-7834)

Vanessa — appreciated. Procurement's ask on a fully non-billed 30d pilot is important for their approval gates. Can you confirm whether we can do that as a one-off for this deal? If so, procurement will likely accept the 12-month commit with a ~10% uplift on discount.

—Alex
